Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, homogeneous opacity in the right upper lung field with smooth margins and no obvious signs of adjacent vessel invasion or pleural effusion. These radiographic features—a sharply defined, non-invasive mass—are characteristic presentations often associated with Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS) in clinical literature, distinguishing it from more invasive primary lung cancers.
